title: Zero and negated currents: integrality, mass of 0 − X, and the bound |X(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·M(X)
statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. (a) The zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_k(U) is integer multiplicity. (b) If X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) is integer multiplicity then so is 0 − X (contract subtraction). (c) M_G(0 − X) = M_G(X) for every X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) and every G ⊆ ℝ^P. (d) If X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with M(X) < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and s > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm), then |X(ω)| ≤ s·M(X), where M(X) is read as a real number via ENNReal.toReal.
lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U k) ∧ (∀ X : GeometricCurrentOn U k, IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity (0 - X)) ∧ (∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (G : Set (Euclid P)), (0 - X).massOn G = X.massOn G) ∧ ∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (ω : TestFormOn U k) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → X.mass ≠ ∞ → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ≤ s) → |X ω| ≤ s * X.mass.toReal
